change.title: stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields

source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses stripe-node 22.1.1 (ai-knowledge-base lockfile) in roughly 35 Next.js apps. stripe-node 23.0.0 pins 2026-09-30.endive.

The one Endive breaking change that hits this repo is the removal of payment_method_types on Checkout Sessions create. Every checkout.sessions.create call site passes it and would get a 400 once on Endive, which would break all checkout flows.

The 23.0.0 removal of constructEventWithoutVerification does not matter, because the repo uses webhooks.constructEvent. Nothing breaks until the SDK or apiVersion is moved, so this is a planned upgrade rather than an outage. The parameter can also be dropped safely today, since dynamic payment methods are the default.

The migration agent should:
- check each app's own package.json and lockfile, because only one lockfile was read;
- make sure any app below v22 instantiates with `new Stripe()`;
- update or remove the explicit apiVersion '2023-10-16' in social-post, and look for other hard-coded apiVersion values in each app's src/lib/stripe.js;
- confirm that webhook handlers reading checkout.session.completed fields still work under Endive (handler code was not read).
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23.0.0 pins 2026-09-30.endive. Bumping the SDK and updating the explicit apiVersion '2023-10-16' in writing_content/social-post/src/lib/stripe.js:9 is the single move that adopts Endive.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout (field-removed): payment_method_types removed from Checkout Sessions create, and paymentMethodTypes option removed from Elements deferred intents (Stripe.js), effective 2026-09-30. Every checkout.sessions.create call in the repo passes payment_method_types. Under Endive this is rejected, so the bump must remove the parameter and rely on dynamic payment methods from the Dashboard.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "We [removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Sessions]"
- stripe:node-22-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed, effective 2026-04-02. ai-knowledge-base is already on 22.1.1. Any app whose own lockfile is still below 22 crosses this major during the bump to 23 and must construct the client with `new Stripe(...)`. The same edit covers it.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:"
- stripe:2026-03-25-dahlia-api-version (api-version): API major 2026-03-25.dahlia with breaking changes (Checkout ui_mode enum values, events_from on event destinations, Capabilities risk requirements, Stripe.js method removals), effective 2026-03-25. social-post pins 2023-10-16, so moving it to Endive also crosses Dahlia. Dahlia's breaking items (ui_mode enum values, events_from, Capabilities) touch none of the recorded call sites, so nothing beyond the pin bump is needed.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "As the first version in the Dahlia release, `2026-03-25.dahlia` introduces both breaking changes and new features"

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');
+const bad=[];
+function walk(d){for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){
+ if(e.name==='node_modules'||e.name==='.next'||e.name==='.git')continue;
+ const p=path.join(d,e.name);
+ if(e.isDirectory())walk(p);
+ else if(/\.(js|jsx|ts|tsx|mjs)$/.test(e.name)){
+  const s=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8');
+  if(/payment_method_types/.test(s)&&/stripe/i.test(s))bad.push(p+': payment_method_types');
+  if(/new Stripe\([^)]*apiVersion/.test(s.replace(/\n/g,' ')))bad.push(p+': apiVersion pin');
+ } else if(e.name==='package.json'){
+  const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8'));
+  const v=(j.dependencies||{}).stripe;
+  if(v&&!v.startsWith('^23.'))bad.push(p+': stripe '+v);
+ }}}
+walk(process.argv[2]||'.');
+if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}
+console.log('ok');

record.prBody:
## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Bumped stripe to ^23.0.0 in all 39 apps that depend on it, using npm install --package-lock-only so only the stripe entry in each lockfile changed. Removed payment_method_types: ["card"] from all 41 checkout.sessions.create call sites. Removed the explicit apiVersion pins: "2023-10-16" in the lib/stripe.js files and "2024-04-10" in the two open-character-ai routes. Those clients now use the SDK's pinned 2026-09-30.endive. Every client already used `new Stripe()`, and every webhook already used webhooks.constructEvent. Nothing uses constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType or V2List. Added scripts/stripe-v23-check.cjs, registered as the check stripe-v23-check. It scans for leftover payment_method_types, apiVersion pins and a stripe dependency below ^23.

Second, it removes `payment_method_types: ["card"]` from `checkout.sessions.create`, which turns on dashboard-managed (dynamic) payment methods. The second edit interacts badly with the existing webhook handler. The 'verified' grade rests on a single check (`stripe-v23-check`) that cannot prove runtime behaviour. The diff is also truncated, so I could not confirm the edits in roughly half the apps or in the two Next.js route files.

concerns.issue: Removing `payment_method_types: ["card"]` is not required by stripe-node 23. It enables whatever payment methods are configured in the Dashboard, which can include delayed-notification methods such as bank debits or vouchers. `handleWebhook` credits the user on `checkout.session.completed` without checking `session.payment_status === 'paid'`. For async methods that event fires with `payment_status: 'unpaid'`, so users could receive credits before (or without) payment. Either restore the line or add a payment_status check plus handling for `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`.

Dropping `apiVersion: "2023-10-16"` silently upgrades every request from 2023-10-16 to the SDK default (stated as 2026-09-30.endive). That spans nearly three years of Stripe API versions with their own breaking changes to Checkout Session and other objects. This is a behavioural change beyond the SDK-major bump, and nothing in the checks exercises a live call. Consider pinning explicitly and reviewing the API changelog between the two versions. I could not confirm the 'endive' version string myself; check the SDK's `apiVersion.ts` or CHANGELOG.

Webhook payload shape is set by the endpoint's API version in the Stripe Dashboard, not by the SDK. After this change the SDK and the webhook endpoint versions may disagree. The handler only reads `metadata`, so the risk is low, but the webhook path is not tested.

The diff is truncated at 60k characters, so I could not see whether these named call sites, or their own Stripe client instantiations, were updated in the same way. If they create their own `new Stripe(...)` with an apiVersion pinned, they would now differ from billing.js.

The lockfiles were regenerated with an npm version that strips the `libc` fields from optional native packages (sharp/img, lightningcss, next-swc, etc.). This is unrelated churn and may change which native binaries are installed on musl or glibc hosts. stripe 23 also raises `engines.node` to >=20; confirm the deploy runtime.

'verified' is based on one static check moving from fail to pass. It does not cover checkout session creation against the new API version, the payment-method change, or webhook handling. Given the unforced behavioural changes above, needs-review would fit better.

checkFirst: Decide whether removing `payment_method_types: ["card"]` is intended. If it is, add a `payment_status === 'paid'` guard and async_payment_succeeded handling in `handleWebhook` before merging.
Confirm that implicitly upgrading from API version 2023-10-16 to the SDK default is acceptable, or pin it explicitly. Check the Stripe API changelog for Checkout changes in between.
View the untruncated diff for the remaining apps and the open-character-ai and Open-AI-UGC route.js files to confirm consistent edits.
Run a test-mode checkout end to end (create session → complete → webhook credits user) on one app.
Verify the deploy Node version is >=20, and that the lockfile libc stripping doesn't break native optional deps in your build image.
